# Description
Analysis of coding variants in SNP context

# Libraries
```{r Libraries, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(gprofiler2)
```

# Loading data
```{r}
loci_in_GRBs <- read_csv("output/loci_in_GRBs_clnv.csv") %>%
  # Maybe remove the next line if it is not there
  select(-X)
clnv <- readRDS("RDS/gnomad_clinvar_df_clean.rds")
```


# loci_clnv
GRB genes and clnv genes are comma separated in columns. loci_clnv contains each grb and clnv gene separated in a row for further analysis. 
```{r}
loci_clnv <- filter(loci_in_GRBs, !is.na(clnv_gene)) %>%
  separate_rows(clnv_gene) %>%
  separate_rows(GRB_GENES)

grb_clnv_match <- filter(loci_clnv, GRB_GENES == clnv_gene)
grb_clnv_match
```
There are 20 terms where mapped_trait, grb_gene and clnv_gene match up and those are:
* squamous cell carcinoma - FGFR2 
* obesity - BDNF
* Tourette syndrome - SOX5
* atrial fibrillation - HCN4
* atrial fibrillation - KCNJ2
* atrial fibrillation - ANK2

The Tourette syndrome SOX5 example shows that searching for parent terms in the ontology could prove beneficial. Other SNPs in the SOX5 GRB are *obsessive compulsive disorder* and *autism spectrum disorder* and all of them share the parent term of *mental disorders*. Furthermore, autism spectrum disorder and Tourette syndrom share a closer parent of *developmental disorder of mental health*. Additionally, an mendelian disease related to SOX5 is *Lamb-Shaffer syndrome* which is a rare disease with various mental and physical abnormalities.  

Idea? Compare all disease terms. Find closest parent term, calculate some distance score. Have a column. disease term, closest parent, some score. 

```{r}
gost_ <- gost(filter(loci_clnv, MAPPED_TRAIT == "autism spectrum disorder") %>% pull(clnv_gene))

gostplot(gost_)
```
